findings.evidence: Lines 18-20 document “equals `2` exactly when the extension is nontrivial”, but lines 71-74 expose only the square-class-independence specialization; lines 75-78 already prove the more general argument from `aut_exponent_dvd_two` (line 57) plus `Monoid.exp_eq_one_iff`.
findings.fix: Add a public theorem such as `aut_exponent_eq_two_of_nontrivial (hroot) [Nontrivial (adjoin K (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[K] adjoin K (Set.range root))] : Monoid.exponent ... = 2`, prove the current independence version from `aut_nontrivial`, and use that as the characteristic API.
findings.issue: `aut_exponent_eq_two` requires `[Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)] [Nonempty ι]` and `hindep`, so consumers with an independently known nontrivial automorphism group cannot use the advertised characterization that the exponent is `2` exactly in the nontrivial case.

summary: The exponent surface is not yet characterized at the right level of generality: it exposes only the square-class-independence corollary, while the stated API is the intrinsic nontrivial case.
